title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout / Go-Live Planning
next_steps: Redwood to share draft runbook and rollback playbook by 2026-11-12
Customer to provision dev PagerDuty channel + Grafana org by 2026-11-13
Schedule 72-hour canary window starting 2026-11-18 with 10% traffic
SE to run smoke test script and share results within 24 hours of canary start
Lena to send pricing/commit options and security pack link by 2026-11-12
action_items: Lena Park - Share SOC2/ISO docs and runbook template - due 2026-11-12
Daniel Kim - Provide smoke test script + sample cURL request and canary config - due 2026-11-13
Maya Singh - Confirm success metrics and final acceptance criteria - due 2026-11-15
Eric Chen - Provision Grafana + Prometheus endpoints and PagerDuty route - due 2026-11-13
Priya Patel - Validate network egress and VPC peering for private deployment - due 2026-11-16
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on rollout planning: agreed on a staged canary (10% -> 50% -> cutover) with a 72-hour canary window, required monitoring dashboards/alerts, and a clear rollback/runbook. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs and security artifacts. Next steps: runbook share, PagerDuty + Grafana provisioning, smoke tests, and scheduling canary start date.
topics: Canary strategy (10% traffic, 72h window, rollout ramps)
A/B vs canary for model variant evaluation
Monitoring and SLOs (latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost)
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm lena from Redwood — we'll kick off, quick agenda: rollout strategy, monitoring, runbook, action items.
[00:14] Maya Singh: hey thanks, quick note we're aiming for go-live late next week if all green, but critical we hit p95 < 120ms and no more than 2% error rate on schema errors.
[00:28] Daniel Kim: got it. On the POC we've been seeing p95 around 95ms on short prompts and 210ms on long chat sessions when KV cache miss, so there's room but within reach with the batching and cache tunes we discussed.
[00:46] Eric Chen: can you remind me though, is that on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated? We haven't finalized infra.
[00:54] Daniel Kim: these numbers are from Dedicated sim on g5-like GPU, in hosted we'd expect similar but depends on multi-tenant burst; for strict SLOs Dedicated gives predictable throughput.
[01:07] Priya Patel: security question — for Private deployment we need KMS integration and audit logs; Hana is on for that.
[01:15] Hana Li: yes we'll need HSM/KMS and SAML SSO enabled, and retention policy for logs 1yr, also SOC2 attest.
[01:24] Lena Park: we'll share the SOC2 pack and the SAML integration doc after this call. Quick check — acceptance criteria recap? Maya?
[01:34] Maya Singh: p95 < 120ms, error rate < 2%, model output quality delta < 3% degradation on our eval set vs baseline, and cost within the committed budget.
[01:44] Tom Brooks: also low hallucination rate on our transactional prompts — that's in the eval set.
[01:50] Daniel Kim: ok for rollout plan proposal: start with a 10% canary for 72 hours, monitor metrics; if stable, ramp to 50% for 24 hours, then cutover. Canary will be an A/B style route where 10% goes to Redwood-optimized model variant and 90% stays on baseline for a/b signals.
[02:12] Eric Chen: i like the staged approach, what are the rollback triggers?
[02:18] Daniel Kim: good question — proposed automatic triggers: p95 increase > 20% vs baseline sustained for 15 minutes, error rate > 3% for 10 minutes, token cost spike > 30% unexpected, or significant regression on quality metrics (we'll tie to automated evals). On trigger we rollback to previous variant and open oncall pager.
[02:37] Priya Patel: define "significant regression" — we need a precise threshold.
[02:42] Maya Singh: for quality let's say > 3% drop in pass@k / eval score or increase in hallucination incidents by 50% over baseline.
[02:51] Daniel Kim: noted. We'll put those thresholds in the runbook.
[02:55] Lena Park: monitoring — what dashboards do you already have?
[03:00] Eric Chen: we've got Grafana with p50/p95, Prometheus metrics, and a baseline errors dashboard. Need Redwood to push model-specific panels and logs.
[03:10] Daniel Kim: we'll share a dashboard JSON and a list of metrics: request_rate, p50, p95, cpu/gpu util, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_latency, error_count, token_cost_per_1000. We'll also include a simple confusion/hallucination counter from your eval webhook.
[03:26] Tom Brooks: for the A/B we want to track user engagement delta too.
[03:29] Lena Park: yes, product metrics should be part of success criteria. We'll capture that in the plan.
[03:36] Hana Li: network — if we do Private, what's required for peering?
[03:40] Daniel Kim: VPC peering and specific CIDR blocks; a minimal set of egress rules. We sent a network requirements doc earlier but we'll resend with exact ports and IPs. Note: in some calls people said "kuberneties" but we mean no need to change k8s, just routing.
[03:58] Eric Chen: any recommended canary duration changes? 72 hours seems long.
[04:02] Maya Singh: we want at least 48 hours but 72 gives better signal for weekend traffic patterns — we prefer 72.
[04:08] Daniel Kim: ok 72 it is. We'll schedule the ramp windows to avoid peak retail hours.
[04:15] Priya Patel: runbook detail — we need step-by-step cutover checklist and rollback steps with exact commands or playbook entries.
[04:22] Daniel Kim: yes we'll include playbook snippets: cutover curl, ingress toggles, scaling policy changes, and the rollback cURL and model pin commands.
[04:30] Lena Park: smoke tests — SE to provide a smoke test script that hits the health endpoint, a few sample prompts, and verification of KV cache warming and latency.
[04:39] Daniel Kim: will do, i'll also include sample curl and a small python script to measure p95 and token usage.
[04:46] Tom Brooks: is A/B going to add extra cost since we run two variants?
[04:50] Lena Park: yes small overhead during A/B but worth it for quality signals; we'll calculate token-based cost and share projected delta in the pricing note.
[04:58] Maya Singh: what about model warming / cold start? we saw a couple of cold-run spikes earlier.
[05:03] Daniel Kim: that's KV cache pre-warm — we'll run warmup traffic before canary cut to reduce cold misses; also we can pre-pin workers if needed on Dedicated.
[05:12] Eric Chen: alerting — where do alerts go? PagerDuty? Slack?
[05:16] Priya Patel: PagerDuty route is required; send critical to oncall pager and also a summary Slack channel.
[05:21] Lena Park: Redwood can push alerts to PagerDuty and Slack, we'll need the routing keys. Add action to provision route.
[05:27] Hana Li: security again — audit logs retention and KMS integration are musts.
[05:31] Lena Park: noted, SOC2 pack will include audit capabilities and KMS patterns.
[05:36] Eric Chen: what about multi-region fallback? If one region degraded, can traffic shift?
[05:40] Daniel Kim: yes we have routing policies for region fallback; we can failover to another region and/or lower-cost model variant. We'll include that in the post-mortem runbook.
[05:49] Tom Brooks: timeline — when can we start the canary?
[05:52] Maya Singh: after runbook and dashboards are set and smoke tests pass — can we aim for 2026-11-18 start?
[05:59] Lena Park: yes we can target 11/18. We'll send calendar hold once we confirm dashboards and PagerDuty.
[06:04] Daniel Kim: i'll run a pre-canary bench on 11/16 to make sure no surprises.
[06:08] Priya Patel: one more — logging: need redact PII from logs.
[06:12] Hana Li: yes we'll provide redaction config, please include in runbook.
[06:16] Lena Park: OK to recap next steps: we'll send runbook, smoke tests, SOC2/security docs, dashboard JSON, and pricing. You (customer) will provision Grafana and PagerDuty, confirm acceptance criteria, and run pre-canary bench.
[06:31] Maya Singh: sounds good.
[06:33] Lena Park: any other q's?
[06:35] Tom Brooks: none from product.
[06:37] Eric Chen: no.
[06:38] Priya Patel: all good.
[06:40] Lena Park: great, thanks everyone — we'll follow up with action items and send invites for the 11/18 canary window once ready.
[06:47] Jose Alvarez: thanks team, we'll be available during the window for support.
[06:50] END OF TRANSCRIPT
